reasoning: I'll skip quoting N for the NAICS breakdown since it double-counts snapshot rows, and the portfolio totals come out to about 49.85% in September versus 46.2% in March. For the six-month view, I'll frame it as March baseline through September, presenting a table with March, June, September, and the change between them.
text:
Revolving-line utilization has been flat at about 46% in 10 of the 12 sectors. Manufacturing and Wholesale Distribution are the exceptions: both have climbed about 3.5 points every month since April and now sit near 69%. That pushed total revolver utilization from 46.2% at March-end to 49.9% at September-end. Nothing else is moving.

**Utilization by sector (drawn ÷ commitment, month-end)**

| Sector | Mar-26 (baseline) | Jun-26 | Sep-26 | Change (pts) | Same-facility change (pts) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Manufacturing** | 46.0% | 58.6% | **69.1%** | **+23.1** | **+23.1** |
| **Wholesale Distribution** | 45.4% | 58.0% | **68.6%** | **+23.2** | **+23.1** |
| CRE Multifamily | 44.5% | 44.3% | 46.2% | +1.7 | +1.3 |
| Healthcare Services | 45.9% | 45.9% | 46.4% | +0.5 | +0.2 |
| Technology | 46.0% | 46.6% | 46.3% | +0.3 | +0.2 |
| Holding & Financial Cos | 46.3% | 46.2% | 46.4% | +0.1 | +0.1 |
| Public & Not-for-Profit | 46.5% | 46.5% | 46.4% | –0.1 | 0.0 |
| Energy | 45.9% | 45.9% | 45.8% | –0.1 | –0.3 |
| Transportation & Logistics | 46.2% | 46.4% | 46.2% | 0.0 | –0.1 |
| Professional Services | 46.4% | 46.1% | 46.3% | –0.1 | –0.2 |
| CRE Office | 46.3% | 46.6% | 46.1% | –0.2 | +0.2 |
| Retail | 46.4% | 45.9% | 46.2% | –0.2 | –0.2 |

The same-facility column only counts lines that existed in both March and September.

**Where it's rising**
- **When it started:** in the 12 months of history, these two sectors held steady at 45.7–46.2% from October 2025 through March 2026. They then rose evenly: 51.3% (Apr), 54.8%, 58.3%, 61.8%, 65.4%, 68.9% (Sep, combined).
- **These are existing borrowers drawing more, not new lines.** On lines that existed in both March and September, drawn balances rose $112.9M in Manufacturing (65 lines) and $75.6M in Wholesale Distribution (44 lines). Every one of those 109 lines rose by more than 5 points.
- **Every industry code in both sectors moved the same way.** Each went from roughly 45–47% to 68–70%: machine shops, industrial machinery, motor-vehicle parts, plastics/resin, grocery wholesale, industrial machinery wholesale and motor-vehicle supplies wholesale.
- **No line is near its limit yet.** The highest single-line utilization in September is about 73%, and no line in either sector is at or above 80%. Only 1 line in these sectors is past due and none are on non-accrual, so this is an early-warning signal and not yet a delinquency problem.
- **Other sectors look flatter-to-higher only because of new lines.** CRE Office, Healthcare, Technology and others added lines in July–September (69 new revolvers bank-wide), but utilization on their existing lines didn't change.

The pattern points to working-capital stress in the auto/industrial supply chain, possibly inventory build or slower receivables. Next steps would be to check borrowing-base and covenant headroom for these borrowers in the risk system and to rank the largest drawn-balance increases.

**Sources and definitions**
- Facility list (`LENDING.FACILITY`): revolvers are product code `RLOC`, "Revolving line of credit" in the product reference table (`REF.PRODUCT`).
- Monthly balances (`LENDING.FACILITY_BAL_MTHLY`): utilization = sum of drawn ÷ sum of (drawn + undrawn), weighted by dollars. Drawn + undrawn matched the commitment on every row, and no line was drawn above its commitment.
- Sector: client industry code (`CORE.CLIENT.NAICS_CD`) mapped through the sector file (`BIZ.SECTOR_MAP`, v4, effective 2024 onward). Every revolver client mapped to a sector.

**Assumptions**
- "Last six months" means April–September 2026, measured against the March 31, 2026 month-end.
- The sector figures include all lines with a balance record that month, including lines later paid off, up to their payoff. The same-facility column covers only lines present in both March and September.
- I didn't use the risk platform; the question only needed the commercial-banking data.
